title: Bezalel the craftsman
hook: Bezalel is filled with spirit to work in gold, stone and wood (Exodus 31:1–5)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was six days: work, then a stop for everyone within the gates. Your line was fairness, written into the week.

The plans are already given: curtains, a chest, a lampstand, a tent of worship, all of it to be made by hand, out in the wilderness. In the book of Exodus, Moses has been shown the design. What they need now is someone who can do the work. A jeweler's eye. A stonemason's straight line. A carpenter's palm that feels what the eye misses. God calls a craftsman by name. Today: Bezalel.
screen: `THE PLANS ARE GIVEN.` → `A TENT TO BE MADE BY HAND.` → `A CRAFTSMAN, CALLED BY NAME.`

segments.voice: First, the call. “See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.” The King James spells it Bezaleel. He's named with his father, his father's father and his tribe. The one who works with his hands is not anonymous labor. He's called by name. Second, the gift. “And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship.” Then the text says what it's for: to work in gold and silver and brass, to cut and set stones, to carve timber. Here the spirit of God doesn't arrive as a vision or a voice. It arrives in the hands. Wisdom, in this chapter, includes knowing how to set a stone straight. Third, the teaching. A few chapters on, the text says he was given it in his heart to teach, he and a partner named Aholiab. The skill isn't a secret to hoard. It's handed on, from one pair of hands to the next. Fourth, the edge from yesterday. Right after Bezalel is named, the same chapter turns back to the sabbath: “Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep.” Some readers, the medieval commentator Rashi among them, take the order as a lesson: even the work of building a holy place stops on the seventh day. So craft, in Exodus, is holy, and it still rests. A careful weld, a well-cut sleeve, a cake with straight layers: a reader of this chapter could call any of them a gift of the spirit.
screen: `CALLED BY NAME.` · `FILLED WITH SPIRIT, FOR CRAFT.` · `GIVEN THE HEART TO TEACH.` · `EVEN HOLY WORK STOPS.` · then, large: `CRAFT IS HOLY.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands and feel them, the fingertips, the palms, the small muscles you only notice when they're tired; these hands have made meals, notes, repairs. Bring to mind one small, real thing they could make today, a sandwich made with care, a sewn-on button, a card, and picture the very first motion. If you pray, you can hold that making in your own tradition's words.
Bezalel. The craftsman called by name in Exodus and filled with the spirit of God to work in gold, stone and wood. Today's word.
Your line: craft is holy. And even holy work rests. That's day eight hundred eighty-three.

howItsDone: Some Jewish and Christian readers point to Bezalel when they speak of craft and art as a gift of the spirit.
